findings.title: The committed suite does not pin that the revoke retries only on transport errors: mutant X49 (retry on any exception) survives the RED file
findings.evidence: X49 replaces `if isinstance(exc, (httpx.HTTPError, asyncio.TimeoutError)): continue / return False` with a bare `continue` in revoke_refresh_token. Run against the RED file (-k r14_ or r27) plus my scratch probe: '1 failed, 13 passed, 141 deselected'. Every RED row passed; the only kill was my probe test_p5_delete_order_with_failing_revoke[non-httpx-raise] ([pyt] tag=b3b-advmut-X49 start=2026-10-17 13:10:40 end=2026-10-17 13:10:48 elapsed=8s status=FAIL rc=1). The implementation itself is correct: with the transport raising a non-httpx exception, probe P5 measured one attempt, the log line '[SIWA] revoke attempt=1 failed: _Boom', and auth_delete still ran (events read_token, cascade, purge x5, revoke, auth_delete). Effect if the mutant shipped: at most one extra bounded 6 s attempt; no data-loss or correctness impact.
findings.fix: Add an R14 case in which the MockTransport handler raises a non-httpx exception (for example RuntimeError) and assert attempts == 1 and the line '[SIWA] revoke attempt=1 failed: RuntimeError'. This is a RED-file amendment for the orchestrator; it does not block this commit.

findings.title: A whitespace-only authorization_code is exchanged at Apple (the gate checks truthiness, not strip)
findings.evidence: Probe test_p4b_str_values_kept with flag ON and config set: '  ' -> 1 request to /auth/token (Apple scripted 400), status 200, body byte-equal to the base body, admin.calls == []. An empty string '' -> 0 requests. A 5,000-character code -> 1 request, 200. Measured: 'PROBE P4b len=2 requests=1 status=200'. The spec gates on `body.authorization_code` being truthy, and B3-A sends only non-empty strings, so this matches the contract. The cost is at most one bounded 6 s Apple call on a malformed body.
findings.fix: Optional: gate on `(body.authorization_code or '').strip()`. No action required for this unit.

findings.title: Key forms outside the accepted three are rejected and fail soft; a quoted Railway paste would silently disable revocation until the canary catches it
findings.evidence:
Probe test_p3_key_forms_with_whitespace accepts (signature verified with the generated public key; exp - iat == 300): a CRLF PEM padded with whitespace, indented PEM lines, a padded literal-
 PEM, a literal-
 PEM with a trailing literal 
, a literal-
 PEM followed by one real trailing newline, base64 with spaces and tabs, base64 wrapped at 64 with CRLF, base64 of a CRLF PEM, and padded base64. Three observation-only forms raise ValueError: a PEM with literal 
, a double-quoted PEM, and a mixed literal plus one real newline. No exception message carries a PEM body line (asserted). In production any of the three would log '[SIWA] client secret build failed: ValueError' and every store and revoke would be skipped; the B4 canary (no 'exchange status=200') is the safety net.
findings.fix: Optional: the owner step in CLAUDE.md and OWNER_ACTIONS could say to paste the value without surrounding quotes.

The working tree stays clean and the index is LF, so there is no diff effect. The other ruff findings in the touched files predate this change (W293, B008, B904, C420, B007, F541 at base lines).
